metadata.name: Asthma
metadata.emergency_level: Chronic - but acute severe/life-threatening asthma is an emergency
metadata.severity: Ranges from mild intermittent to severe; acute attacks can be fatal

overview.short_description: A chronic inflammatory airway disorder with variable, reversible airflow obstruction and bronchial hyper-responsiveness, causing episodic wheeze, cough, chest tightness and breathlessness.
overview.detailed_description: Asthma is common and typically atopic, beginning in childhood but presenting at any age. Its hallmark is VARIABLE, often reversible airflow limitation. Diagnosis combines a compatible history with objective tests (spirometry with reversibility, FeNO, peak-flow variability, bronchial challenge). Management is stepwise inhaled therapy (now anchored on inhaled-corticosteroid-containing regimens), self-management with a personalised action plan, and prompt treatment of exacerbations. Recognising and treating acute severe/life-threatening attacks is critical.
overview.pathophysiology: Chronic airway inflammation (eosinophilic and/or other) causes bronchial hyper-responsiveness; triggers provoke bronchoconstriction, mucosal oedema and mucus, producing reversible airflow obstruction. Chronic uncontrolled inflammation can lead to airway remodelling.
overview.etiology: Multifactorial: atopy/allergen sensitisation, genetic predisposition, respiratory infections, environmental exposures. Common triggers: allergens, viral infections, exercise, cold air, smoke/pollution, NSAIDs/beta-blockers, occupational agents.
overview.natural_history: Variable; childhood asthma may remit or persist; adult-onset also occurs. Well-controlled patients have normal lives; poor control risks exacerbations and, rarely, death.
overview.prognosis: Good with adherence and correct inhaler technique; poor control and under-use of inhaled corticosteroids increase exacerbation and mortality risk.

prevalence.value: Affects an estimated ~260 million people worldwide (GINA/WHO); common in children and adults.

mortality.value: WHO estimates hundreds of thousands of asthma deaths yearly, many preventable.

epidemiology.sex_predominance: More common in boys in childhood; shifts towards females in adulthood.
epidemiology.geographic_distribution: Worldwide; higher prevalence in many high-income and urbanising settings.
epidemiology.seasonal_pattern: Exacerbations peak with viral seasons and relevant allergen seasons.

risk_factors.lifestyle: Allergen and pollutant exposure, physical inactivity/obesity.
risk_factors.smoking: Active and passive smoke worsen control and accelerate decline; maternal smoking increases childhood asthma.
risk_factors.obesity: Associated with asthma and worse control.
risk_factors.hypertension: Not a risk factor (but beta-blockers can worsen asthma).
risk_factors.pregnancy: Control can change; maintaining control is important for mother and baby.
risk_factors.occupation: Occupational asthma from workplace sensitisers (flour, isocyanates, animals, latex).
risk_factors.medications: NSAIDs/aspirin and non-selective beta-blockers can trigger bronchospasm in susceptible patients.
risk_factors.previous_diseases: Eczema, allergic rhinitis (atopic march); recurrent childhood wheeze.

chief_complaints.complaint: Cough, often worse at night/early morning
chief_complaints.importance: May be the main symptom (cough-variant asthma)

symptoms.symptom: Cough, worse at night/early morning or with exercise/cold
Diurnal variability and symptoms with specific triggers
symptoms.importance: VARIABILITY and trigger-relationship strongly support asthma

symptoms.symptom: Silent chest, exhaustion, cyanosis, altered consciousness (severe attack)

negative_findings.finding: Truly fixed, non-variable symptoms with no reversibility and heavy smoking history
No symptom variability, normal spirometry/PEF variability, and negative FeNO/reversibility
negative_findings.why_important: Reduces the likelihood of asthma (though not fully excluded)

history_questions.question: Are symptoms episodic and variable, worse at night/early morning, and triggered by allergens/exercise/cold/infection?
history_questions.why_ask: Variability and triggers are central to diagnosing asthma

history_questions.question: Do symptoms improve with a bronchodilator?
Personal/family history of atopy (eczema, hay fever, allergies)?
How often do you use your reliever inhaler and have you had oral steroid courses/attacks/admissions?
history_questions.why_ask: Assesses control and future-risk (over-reliance on reliever is high-risk)

history_questions.question: Do you smoke, and any occupational exposures, NSAID/beta-blocker use?

physical_examination.expected_finding: Widespread expiratory wheeze (often normal between episodes)

physical_examination.examination: Respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, ability to speak (in acute attack)

physical_examination.expected_finding: Reduced/variable; used to grade acute severity

vital_signs.heart_rate: May be raised in an exacerbation; bradycardia is a life-threatening sign
vital_signs.respiratory_rate: Raised in exacerbation; a key severity marker
vital_signs.oxygen_saturation: Normal when well; <92% indicates severe/life-threatening attack

laboratory_tests.test_name: Blood eosinophils / total IgE / allergen testing (selective)

imaging.when_needed: Diagnostic uncertainty, atypical features, or to exclude complications in a severe exacerbation (e.g., pneumothorax, infection)
imaging.expected_findings: Often normal; hyperinflation in acute attack

ecg.when_needed: In severe exacerbation or to assess cardiac differential
ecg.findings: Sinus tachycardia; helps exclude cardiac cause of breathlessness.

other_diagnostic_tests.spirometry: Spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility is central: obstructive pattern (reduced FEV1/FVC) with significant reversibility supports asthma.
other_diagnostic_tests.endoscopy: Not applicable (bronchoscopy only for specific indications)
other_diagnostic_tests.peak_flow: Serial peak-flow monitoring showing diurnal variability supports asthma; bronchial challenge testing in uncertain cases.

diagnostic_criteria.formal_criteria: Compatible symptoms (episodic, variable wheeze/breathlessness/cough/chest tightness) PLUS objective evidence of variable airflow limitation: bronchodilator reversibility on spirometry (e.g., improvement in FEV1), raised FeNO, peak-flow variability, or a positive bronchial challenge. No single test is definitive; guidelines (GINA; BTS/NICE/SIGN NG245) advise a structured objective work-up.
diagnostic_criteria.diagnostic_scores: Control assessed with tools such as the Asthma Control Test/RCP 3 questions; not diagnostic.

cutoff_values.value: NICE: FeNO >=40 ppb (adults) supportive; obstructive spirometry FEV1/FVC <0.7 with reversibility (e.g., FEV1 improvement >=12% and 200 mL) supportive; PEF variability >20%.

differential_diagnosis.differences: Older, smoker, persistent (less variable) airflow limitation, minimal reversibility
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Are symptoms variable/reversible or steadily progressive with a smoking history?

differential_diagnosis.differences: Orthopnoea, oedema, cardiac history, basal crackles
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Do you get breathless lying flat with ankle swelling?

differential_diagnosis.disease: Vocal cord dysfunction / inducible laryngeal obstruction
differential_diagnosis.differences: Inspiratory noise, throat tightness, poor response to bronchodilator
differential_diagnosis.differential_questions: Is the tightness in your throat with noisy breathing in?
Do you cough up sputum most days with repeated chest infections?
Did it start suddenly after an exposure, with rash or swelling?

diagnostic_questions.question: Are your symptoms variable - worse at night/early morning and with specific triggers - and do they improve with a reliever inhaler?
diagnostic_questions.purpose: Variability + reversibility is the core discriminator

diagnostic_questions.question: In an acute attack: can you complete sentences, what is your oxygen level and peak flow?
diagnostic_questions.interpretation: Inability to speak, SpO2 <92%, low PEF, silent chest -> life-threatening

next_best_question.question: Are your symptoms variable and trigger-related, and how often do you use your reliever?
next_best_question.branching_logic: Typical pattern -> objective testing (spirometry+reversibility, FeNO, PEF) and start ICS-based treatment; frequent reliever use -> escalate and review technique/adherence

next_best_test.test: Spirometry with bronchodilator reversibility (+ FeNO / peak-flow diary)
next_best_test.why: Objective evidence of variable airflow limitation

red_flags.finding: Silent chest, cyanosis, exhaustion, poor respiratory effort, altered consciousness, bradycardia, or SpO2 <92%
red_flags.immediate_action: Life-threatening asthma - emergency: high-flow oxygen, nebulised salbutamol/ipratropium, systemic steroids, urgent senior/critical-care help

red_flags.finding: Cannot complete sentences, RR >=25, HR >=110, PEF 33-50% predicted
red_flags.immediate_action: Acute severe asthma - urgent treatment and assessment

red_flags.finding: Poor response to initial treatment or rising CO2
Frequent reliever use, prior near-fatal attack, or multiple recent courses of oral steroids
red_flags.immediate_action: High-risk - urgent review and treatment escalation

referral_criteria.urgent_referral: Acute severe/life-threatening exacerbation (emergency); diagnostic uncertainty needing specialist testing.
referral_criteria.routine_referral: Poor control despite optimised treatment and good adherence/technique; suspected occupational asthma; consideration of biologics/severe-asthma assessment.
referral_criteria.emergency_referral: Life-threatening asthma or failure to respond to acute treatment.

late: Steroid-related effects with frequent oral courses

initial_management.supportive_care: Confirm diagnosis objectively; personalised asthma action plan; inhaler technique and adherence checks; trigger avoidance; smoking cessation; annual review.
initial_management.medications: Canonical schema 1.3 guidance: use treatment_guidance.medication_options and its history-based safety checks. Candidate classes/options (not a prescription): ICS-containing inhaler regimen; Bronchodilator reliever; Short systemic corticosteroid course; Add-on LAMA/LTRA/biologic. No autonomous selection or dosing is allowed. Source IDs: NICE_NG245.
initial_management.lifestyle_advice: Stop smoking, avoid triggers, maintain healthy weight and activity, ensure vaccinations (influenza), correct inhaler technique.
initial_management.follow_up: Review after exacerbations and at least annually; assess control (symptoms, reliever use, exacerbations, lung function) and step treatment up/down.
initial_management.legacy_medications_pre_v13: Anchor treatment on inhaled corticosteroid (ICS)-containing therapy - modern guidance (GINA) does NOT recommend short-acting beta-agonist (SABA)-only treatment. Use ICS-formoterol as reliever (+/- maintenance) or regular ICS with a reliever, stepping up to ICS/LABA and add-ons (LAMA, LTRA) as needed; biologics for severe eosinophilic/allergic asthma. Acute exacerbation: oxygen to target saturations, inhaled/nebulised bronchodilators, systemic corticosteroids, +/- ipratropium/magnesium per severity.

patient_education.home_advice: Asthma is a long-term condition where the airways are sensitive and can tighten. The key is using your preventer (steroid) inhaler every day as prescribed - not just relying on your blue reliever. Learn your inhaler technique, follow your written action plan, and know the danger signs. Get emergency help if your reliever isn't working, you're too breathless to speak, or your lips look blue.
patient_education.home_advice_ar: الربو حالة مزمنة تكون فيها المجاري الهوائية حسّاسة وقد تضيق. الأساس هو استخدام بخاخ الوقاية (الستيرويد) يومياً كما وُصف - لا الاعتماد على البخاخ الموسّع الأزرق فقط. أتقن طريقة استخدام البخاخ، والتزم بخطة العمل المكتوبة، واعرف علامات الخطر. اطلب المساعدة الطارئة إذا لم يعُد البخاخ الموسّع يُجدي، أو عجزت عن الكلام من ضيق النفس، أو ازرقّت شفتاك.
patient_education.prevention: Trigger avoidance, smoking cessation, good adherence to preventer therapy, influenza vaccination.
patient_education.warning_signs: Reliever not lasting/working, too breathless to speak or eat, blue lips, exhaustion, or peak flow falling sharply - seek emergency care.

prevention.vaccination: Annual influenza vaccination (and pneumococcal per local guidance).
prevention.lifestyle: Avoid tobacco smoke and known triggers; healthy weight and activity.

evidence.evidence_level: High - large trials/guidelines support ICS-based therapy and against SABA-only treatment.
evidence.guideline_strength: The main diagnosis/test and treatment direction was checked against the current guidance identified by NICE_NG245; see evidence_review for scope and limitations. This does not verify every legacy narrative sentence.
